chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musanna al-Hannat, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A man intends to give the full measure, but when he measures, he is not good at measuring.' He said, 'So what do those around him say?' I said, 'They say,
He does not give the full measure.
He said, 'This one, it is not befitting for him that he measures.'

key_terms.لَا يَنْبَغِي: It is not befitting / Not suitable

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a merchant who intends to give full measure but lacks the skill to do so accurately?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between mere intention (*niyyah*) and technical competence (*maharah*) in trade, ruling that a person who cannot measure accurately should refrain from the act to avoid unintentional injustice (*zulm*). This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the objective validity of transactions, where skill is a prerequisite for fulfilling the ethical duty of giving full measure. The Imam’s directive serves as a practical safeguard against the common commercial sin of short-changing, even by the well-meaning.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musna Al Hannat, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man intends the full measurement, and he, when he weighs, is not good at it in weighing’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So what are they saying, those who are around him?’ I said, ‘They are saying, ‘He does no give full measure’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This one, it is not befitting for him that he weighs’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Muthanna’ al-Hannat from certain persons of our people who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘There is man who has the intention to maintain proper weighing; but when he weighs cannot do it properly.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘What do people around say about him?’ I (the narrator) replied, ‘They say, ‘He does not maintain it properly.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘He should not do weighing.’”
